newsitem.title: UK: Licht sees stable world raw sugar demand in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Licht sees stable world raw sugar demand in 96/97.

text.p: World demand for raw sugar is expected to be stable at 19 million tonnes in the 1996/97 (September/August) crop year, roughly the same as last year, statistican F.O. Licht said on Wednesday.
"The outlook for the raws market looks to be less bleak (than for the whites)," Licht said in its first estimate of the global 1996/97 sugar balance.
"However, there is no reason to believe supplies will not be completely adequate to meet this requirement unless there are some unforeseen calamities," it said.
Licht said one welcome sign from the United States was that imports of raws for refining for the domestic market were expected to increase, but gave no further details.

It estimated world 1996/97 imports at 35.41 million tonnes, 1.98 million tonnes lower than the previous year, adding that the white sugar sector had most reason to be concerned about the expected fall.
